title: The Present Participle Active
subtitle: λύων, λύουσα, λῦον — the verbal adjective.
objectives: Form and decline the present active participle of any ω-verb.
Understand the participle as a verbal adjective with tense and voice.
Use the participle in attributive and circumstantial constructions.

sections.heading: The participle
sections.body:
The participle is a verbal adjective. It has the tense and voice of a verb (present, aorist, future; active, middle, passive). It declines like an adjective and agrees with a noun in gender, number, and case.

The present active participle means 'doing X' or 'while doing X' or 'the one who does X'. λύων means 'loosing' or 'the one who is loosing'. It has three genders: masculine λύων, feminine λύουσα, neuter λῦον.

sections.heading: The present active participle: λύων, λύουσα, λῦον
sections.body:
Masculine (third declension):
              singular        plural
  nominative  λύων            λύοντες
  genitive    λύοντος         λυόντων
  dative      λύοντι          λύουσι(ν)
  accusative  λύοντα          λύοντας

Feminine (first declension):
              singular        plural
  nominative  λύουσα          λύουσαι
  genitive    λυούσης         λυουσῶν
  dative      λυούσῃ          λυούσαις
  accusative  λύουσαν         λυούσας

Neuter (third declension):
              singular        plural
  nominative  λῦον            λύοντα
  genitive    λύοντος         λυόντων
  dative      λύοντι          λύουσι(ν)
  accusative  λῦον            λύοντα

The stem is λυοντ- for masculine and neuter. The feminine is formed from the same stem with first-declension endings.

sections.heading: Uses of the participle
sections.body:
Attributive: ὁ λύων ἀνήρ — 'the man who is loosing' or 'the loosing man'.

Circumstantial: λύων τοὺς αἰχμαλώτους ἀπῆλθεν — 'loosing the prisoners, he went away' or 'while he was loosing the prisoners, he went away'.

Supplementary: φαίνεται λύων — 'he appears to be loosing'. Some verbs take a supplementary participle to complete their meaning.

sections.heading: From Xenophon
sections.body:
Anabasis I.2.1: ἐξελαύνων διὰ τῆς Λυδίας.
'Marching through Lydia' or 'while he was marching through Lydia'. ἐξελαύνων is the present active participle of ἐξελαύνω.

items.answer: genitive singular masculine or neuter of λύων
the man who is loosing / the loosing man
While loosing the prisoners, he went away.
A verbal adjective with tense and voice.

words.gloss: the man who is freeing the prisoners

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 3.11 introduces the aorist participle active. The aorist participle expresses completed action: λύσας means 'having loosed'. It is used for antecedent action — action that happened before the main verb.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can form and decline the present active participle of any ω-verb and can translate participles in attributive and circumstantial use.
